entries.what_happened: Manuscript 'Positivity of Serre's Intersection Multiplicity' (build/paper.tex, dated September 23, 2026). Its Theorem 1.1 (thm:main) claims: for a commutative Noetherian regular local ring (R, m) of dimension d, and nonzero finitely generated R-modules M, N with length(M tensor N) < infinity and dim M + dim N = d, the Serre multiplicity chi^R(M,N) = sum_i (-1)^i length Tor_i^R(M,N) is strictly positive. The abstract and introduction say this proves Serre's positivity conjecture with no restriction on characteristic or ramification, and without requiring either module to lift to an unramified base. Taking M = R/P and N = R/Q gives the list's statement. The proof (sections lengths, descent, asymptotic, positivity) reduces to complete domain pairs D = R/P, E = R/Q of dimensions h, l > 0 with h + l = d, over a complete base with algebraically closed residue field of characteristic p > 0; the equicharacteristic case is attributed to Serre. It then builds normalized-length algebras C_D and C_E over regular normalization bases, equates ordinary and normalized Euler sums over Galois conjugates (supported rational descent, Theorem ds:descent; asymptotic norm comparison, Theorem as:norm), and shows each term is positive using a uniform lower bound on minimal generator counts. Separately, Corollary cor:tangent-cone (introduction, 'Consequences') states chi^A(A/P,A/Q) >= e(A/P) e(A/Q) for primes P, Q of a regular local A with A/(P+Q) of finite length, complementary dimensions and dim T <= 1, with equality iff dim T = 0. The same section derives from Theorem 1.1, via Kurano--Roberts, the containment P cap Q^(r) contained in m^(r+1) for r >= 1, for ramified R with sqrt(P+Q) = m and ht P + ht Q = dim R.
entries.delivers: If correct, establishes the list's statement for every commutative regular local ring: for primes P, Q with dim R/P + dim R/Q = dim R, chi(R/P,R/Q) > 0, with no restriction on characteristic, ramification or lifting. The manuscript says it proves the conjecture. Its statement matches the list's in two respects that differ: (a) it adds the hypothesis length(R/(P+Q)) < infinity, i.e. P+Q is m-primary, which chi needs in order to be defined and which the list's wording leaves implicit; (b) it proves Serre's module form, which is more general than the prime-quotient form the list asks about. Otherwise the statement matches: nonzero, finitely generated, commutative Noetherian regular local ring, with strict positivity as the conclusion. No dimension range, bound or counterexample is involved.
entries.remains: If the claim holds, nothing in the bullet or in problem_asks (1)-(4) remains open. Outside the claim: prime pairs with R/(P+Q) of infinite length, for which chi is undefined and the list's inequality has no content. The corollary and the symbolic-power consequence in the introduction are additional statements, not parts of the list's problem.
entries.direction: proves the conjecture (strict positivity for all regular local rings, mixed characteristic and ramified case included)
entries.conditional_on: No hypothesis beyond the theorem's own. The argument does rely on published results it cites rather than proves: the Roberts and Gillet-Soule vanishing theorem (pos:vanishing, used in the reduction); Serre's theorem for the equicharacteristic case; Cohen-Gabber normalization in characteristic p (cited via Kurano-Shimomoto); in mixed characteristic, the perfectoid length results of Cai-Lee-Ma-Schwede-Tucker (Cor. 4.0.4, Props. 4.0.10 and 4.0.14, on Bhatt-Scholze Prop. 8.5) and Faltings' normalized-length formalism; in characteristic p, Roberts' Frobenius homology theorem (as stated in Ma, Thm. 2.4) and Monsky's Hilbert-Kunz existence theorem; and Land-Tamme truncating descent with Goodwillie, Thomason-Trobaugh and BGT for the K-theory inputs. The only OpenAI manuscript cited is OpenAILech2026 (Lech's multiplicity conjecture), cited in lengths.tex for related normalized-length constructions; the text does not say the proof depends on it. The corollary depends on Skalit's SkalitUnramified lemmas, and the symbolic-power consequence on Kurano-Roberts Thm. 3.2; both are cited, not reproved.
entries.doubts: The text flags no step as sketched, but it compresses or cites several key steps. (1) The mixed-characteristic input (Theorem len:input, mixed case) is one short paragraph. It says 'the stated hypotheses there are exactly' those of CLMST and Bhatt-Scholze, then applies their results to C_D without checking those hypotheses in the text. (2) Several structural lemmas are argued in a few sentences: residue-field extension (len:residue-extension), normalization (len:normalization), the tower and its length (len:tower), and the orbit argument in the descent proof. In len:normalization the positive-characteristic case, including generic separability of A in D, is attributed to Cohen-Gabber, with no separate argument for the separability clause. (3) Statement and proof differ in Theorem ds:descent: it states that the K_0 map is surjective, but its proof concludes that it is an isomorphism ('in fact as an isomorphism'). The text does not reconcile the two. (4) Corollary cor:tangent-cone assumes dim T <= 1, which the proof uses only implicitly, to assert that S is finite. It applies lemmas from Skalit's SkalitUnramified, whose title is 'in the unramified case', to a general regular A, and does not say why the unramified hypothesis is unnecessary. (5) The symbolic-power consequence is introduced with 'now gives' via Kurano-Roberts Thm. 3.2, without restating that theorem's hypotheses. (6) Footnote 1 records a public post dated December 9, 2025 by Editan, credited also to Copilot and Gemini, asserting the same prime-quotient form. The authors record it as a same-scope claim, 'not as an established theorem', and give no further account of it.

entries.what_happened: Same manuscript and Theorem 1.1 as in the Serre entry. Of the bullet's named items, it bears only on item (13), Serre's conjecture on multiplicities, and only on its positivity half: it proves strict positivity of chi^R(M,N) over all regular local rings, for nonzero finitely generated modules with finite-length tensor product and complementary dimensions. The vanishing half (chi = 0 when the dimensions sum to less than d) is not claimed here. The paper cites it as known (Roberts 1985; Gillet-Soule 1987; pos:vanishing) and uses it in its reduction. None of items (1)-(12) or (14) is stated, proved or discussed. The conjectures in the matching note that lie beyond the article's own list (Peskine-Szpiro dimension, grade and strong intersection; Huneke-Sega-Vraciu Tor vanishing; Huneke-Wiegand; Auslander-Reiten, Nakayama and Tachikawa) do not appear in the text. The only 'Tor-vanishing' in the text is a liftability hypothesis attributed to KC and Soto Levins in the introduction, not the Huneke-Sega-Vraciu conjecture.
entries.delivers: Strict positivity of Serre's intersection multiplicity for all commutative Noetherian regular local rings, mixed characteristic and ramified case included, for nonzero finitely generated modules M, N with length(M tensor N) < infinity and dim M + dim N = d. This is the positivity assertion of item (13), in Serre's module form. Restrictions: the finite-length hypothesis, and positivity only, not vanishing. The item's wording covers 'vanishing and positivity of intersection multiplicities for regular R'; the manuscript matches the positivity half only.
entries.remains: If the claim holds: within item (13), the vanishing part is not claimed here (the paper uses a published vanishing theorem), so it is not a result of this family. Items (1)-(12) and (14) are untouched. The other conjectures of the wider literature, if they fall within the bullet's scope (Peskine-Szpiro dimension, grade and strong intersection; Huneke-Sega-Vraciu; Huneke-Wiegand; Auslander-Reiten, Nakayama and Tachikawa), are untouched too.
entries.direction: proves the positivity part of item (13), in full generality for regular local rings (not a special case)
entries.conditional_on: No hypothesis beyond the theorem's own. The proof relies on published results it cites rather than proves: the Roberts and Gillet-Soule vanishing theorems (used in the reduction); Serre's theorem for the equicharacteristic case; and, for the mixed-characteristic core, the perfectoid normalized-length results of Cai-Lee-Ma-Schwede-Tucker built on Bhatt-Scholze, together with Land-Tamme descent and Faltings' normalized-length formalism. The only OpenAI manuscript cited is OpenAILech2026 (Lech's multiplicity conjecture), cited in lengths.tex for related normalized-length constructions; the text does not say the proof depends on it.
entries.doubts: Same as the Serre entry. The text flags no step as sketched, but the mixed-characteristic core is one paragraph that asserts the cited hypotheses without checking them in the text; several structural lemmas are compressed; the descent theorem states surjectivity while its proof concludes isomorphism; the corollary applies lemmas from a paper titled 'in the unramified case' to a general regular base; and footnote 1 records a December 9, 2025 post by others asserting the prime-quotient form, which the authors do not treat as established. Scope: the manuscript's claim concerns item (13) only, and it does not address the bullet's other items.
